reusable_cues.rationale: Worst-class-first repair is a reusable cue for a defect-class elimination loop.

source_text:
## HEAD

The "killer idea" (golden-walk-ledger.md §THE KILLER IDEA), made operational:
mine the math corpus **structure-first** — concepts are the index, papers are
occurrence sites — and run a **Distributed-Proofreaders** loop over it:
mine → measure loss → fix the worst class → re-mine, anytime, never perfect.
Named for the volunteer book-digitisation model: systematic per-type passes,
each pass clearing one defect class, quality a property of the revision
process rather than any single snapshot (the Moran-1971 *because*-clause
lesson, futon5a/essays/moran-1971-agent-cascades).

sentences.unresolved_reason: Section marker only; no interpretable move.

fragments.text: The "killer idea" (golden-walk-ledger.md §THE KILLER IDEA), made operational:
fragments.target: the killer idea from golden-walk-ledger.md, now to be made operational in this mission
fragments.rationale: The HEAD declares intent: a previously recorded idea is to become working infrastructure, not stay an essay. This is the mission's anchor claim, stated as operator voice, not evidence the idea is yet operational.

pattern_refs.rationale: The phrase 'made operational' sets the test this pattern names: the artifact must change behaviour when it fails, not merely document the idea.

fragments.text: mine the math corpus **structure-first** — concepts are the index
fragments.target: the mining order: corpus structure before corpus text, with concepts as the primary index
fragments.rationale: The first operational move inverts the usual mining order: instead of indexing papers and extracting concepts, concepts are the index and papers become secondary sites where a concept occurs.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern makes an external index the system of record for projects; here the move is about inverting what indexes what inside one corpus, not designating an external register.
pattern_rejections.query: index by concepts, documents are occurrence sites

fragments.text: occurrence sites — and run a **Distributed-Proofreaders** loop over it
fragments.target: a Distributed-Proofreaders loop run over the concept-indexed corpus
fragments.rationale: Completes the inversion (papers demoted to occurrence sites) and commissions the named loop as the engine that works over that structure.

fragments.text: mine → measure loss → fix the worst class → re-mine, anytime, never perfect.
fragments.target: the mine/measure/fix/re-mine loop, run continuously without a perfection gate
fragments.rationale: The loop's shape: each cycle measures loss, eliminates the single worst defect class, and re-mines; 'anytime, never perfect' makes quality emergent from iteration rather than a launch condition.

pattern_refs.rationale: Fixing the worst defect class per pass mirrors this pattern's discipline: treat failure classes as defects to eliminate systematically, with the shrinking class census as the metric.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern asks whether the system itself can perceive its regulation target; this loop is steered by an external operator measuring loss, so self-perception of the objective is not the crux.
pattern_rejections.query: iterative loop: measure the loss, fix the worst defect class, re-run, never perfect

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern governs re-entering a paused line of work after an observed repair; the HEAD's loop is a continuous mining cadence, not a suspend/resume discipline.
pattern_rejections.query: iterative loop: measure the loss, fix the worst defect class, re-run, never perfect

fragments.text: Named for the volunteer book-digitisation model: systematic per-type passes
fragments.target: the loop's name, borrowed from the volunteer book-digitisation model of per-type passes
fragments.rationale: The naming imports a proven social model: many volunteers each clearing one error type across the whole corpus, which legitimises the per-defect-class pass structure.

fragments.text: each pass clearing one defect class, quality a property of the revision
fragments.target: where quality lives: in the revision process, one cleared defect class per pass
fragments.rationale: The epistemic claim of the HEAD: quality is not a snapshot property but accrues from the revision process itself, pass by pass.

pattern_refs.rationale: The living-document-versus-snapshot distinction matches: the HEAD subordinates any frozen snapshot to the continuously revised artefact, exactly the cadence this pattern makes declarable.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern elevates periodic point-in-time snapshots as the queryable evidence; the HEAD explicitly demotes snapshots in favour of the process, so citing it would invert the claim.
pattern_rejections.query: quality is a property of the revision process not a single snapshot

fragments.text: process rather than any single snapshot (the Moran-1971 *because*-clause
fragments.target: revision process contrasted against any single snapshot, per the Moran-1971 because-clause
fragments.rationale: The contrast half of the quality claim, with its cited warrant: Moran-1971's because-clause lesson is the named source for trusting process over snapshot.
The evidence pointer closing the because-clause citation; it grounds the process-over-snapshot claim in a named essay rather than asserting it bare.
